One hundred years ago, the word�psychology�was a strange new word to the average person. Today, people use it frequently to describe events in their everyday lives. Books on psychology line the shelves of many bookstores. Drugstores display magazines with many articles on psychology-related subjects. Even comics and television shows deal with psychoanalysis, I.Q.s, and hypnosis.



Why has psychology gained such popularity?

The answer is fairly simple. The study of psychology is the study of our selves. From earliest times, people have been curious about their own nature. For example, they wondered what actually happened in their dreams when they would visit faraway places or do impossible things like flying through the air. Yet when they awoke, they would be in the same place where they had lain down to sleep. How could that be explained? Was there an invisible person inside who took these journeys while the body remained behind? What left the body when people died and ceased to breathe, to talk, to laugh and to touch?

Gradually, from these questions, the idea of a soul developed. The ancient Greeks named this concept the�psyche�which means the mind or the soul. The Greek word�logia�means the study of something. Therefore,�psychology�is the study of the mind.


Psychology is the study of the mind and its various faculties. Long ago, people believed that the mind existed separately from the body. As the study of psychology developed, investigations were limited to the study of�consciousness.�Consciousness�is what a person feels, thinks, or is aware of in some way, like colours, shape, smell pain, or other sensations. Soon, however the definition of psychology as the study of consciousness proved to be inadequate. Why was this true? It was found that a good deal of behavior and even a certain amount of thinking took place beneath the conscious level of the mind  in a realm now called the�unconscious. Today, the meaning of psychology has been broadened to include the study of all behavior, whether conscious or unconscious. We now define psychology as�the science of human behavior.
